channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: What a Democratic Congress Means for Trump’s Foreign-Policy Agenda
item.description: From Iran to trade, here is what the reshaped House and Senate could mean for the president’s signature policies.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of November 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: Oil Prices Fall as Investors Weigh U.S. Midterm Results, Iran Risks
item.description: Oil prices extended losses Wednesday as investors weighed the Democrats’ sweep of Congress and the implications for Trump’s approach to Iran.

item.title: Democrats Take Congress as Trump Says Iran War Is Partly to Blame for GOP Losses
item.description: Plus, Iran turns to guerrilla tactics to try to stop the flow of oil leaving the Strait of Hormuz, and CVS Health decides to split in two.

item.title: Sweden’s Central Bank Latest to Lift Rates in Response to War
item.description: Sweden’s central bank raised its key interest rate for the first time since the start of the war between the U.S. and Iran, and signaled that more increases in borrowing costs were likely.

item.title: North Korea, on Busiest Missile-Testing Spree in Years, Rebuffs Trump Diplomacy
item.description: The regime launched a fresh salvo as it spurns U.S. diplomatic overtures with a growing list of demands.

item.title: Once a Haven for Guerrillas, Venezuela Now Helps U.S. Attack Them
item.description: Venezuela’s government, which sheltered rebels for decades, cooperated in a recent deadly drone strike as Washington and Caracas forge closer military ties.

item.title: Hackers Crank the Heat on Europe’s Supermarket Freezers to Above 120 Degrees
item.description: As more everyday items are plugged into the internet, hackers have a vast new menu of targets to choose from.

item.title: Iran Turns to Guerrilla Tactics in Bid to Reassert Grip on Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Tehran is deploying everything from rocket-propelled grenades to limpet mines as it attempts to disrupt the restored flow of oil out of the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Latest U.S.-Canada Trade Talks Yield Progress Toward Pact, Carney Says
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said the U.S. is “asking less and offering more” in the latest round of negotiations, though major hurdles remain.

item.title: Democrats and Republicans Battle for Control of Congress
item.description: Plus, Trump says the U.S. plans to cut off military aid to Israel by the end of the year, and some Learjet wreckage was found miles away from the crash site.

item.title: Trump Says U.S. Plans to Cut Off Military Aid to Israel by End of Year
item.description: The U.S. and Israel have discussed phasing out grants, but the president’s comments suggest it could occur much faster than expected.

item.title: Oil Futures Turn Lower as Market Holds Out Hope for Middle East Diplomacy
item.description: Oil futures settled lower in a choppy session, with concerns about U.S. strikes on Iranian targets cushioned by continued diplomatic efforts to bring the U.S. and Iran to a conflict settlement.

item.title: ‘Broken China’ Review: A Mirage of Growth
item.description: Beijing touts rosy statistics, but China’s leaders have clogged the country’s banks and local governments with unproductive investments.

item.title: El Salvador’s President Takes a High-Stakes Gamble Confronting Haitian Gangs
item.description: The deployment of 2,500 Salvadoran troops in lawless Haiti could raise the risk of an urban combat quagmire.

item.title: Britain Set to Apologize for Role in Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade
item.description: The U.K., which played major role in trans-Atlantic slave trade but also ended it, says it won’t pay reparations.

item.title: Eager to Rebut Rogue-Nation Image, North Korea Denies Role in Binance Heist
item.description: In an unusual move for Pyongyang, Kim Jong Un’s powerful sister issued a swift rebuttal of any role in the $6.3 billion hack.

item.title: The Little-Known Chinese Bank in the Middle of Iranian and Russian Money Flows
item.description: China has emerged as a key hub for illicit money flows, but Washington is reluctant to crack down, officials say.

item.title: NATO’s New Defense Plan Would Mean Strikes Deep Inside Russia
item.description: Commanders say precise long-range weapons are core to deterring Moscow from attacking the alliance.

item.title: Russian Airstrike Kills 31 at Ukraine Aid Center
item.description: Dozens are missing after an attack at a school in southern Ukraine where humanitarian aid was being handed out.
